title: Backtesting is Way Different from Live Trading

Size up on A+ setups: study your best patterns, use technology to find more of them

Trade small until proof of concept; 150% of daily stop on a new strategy is unacceptable
Overconfidence after good results is a leading cause of outsized losses on new ideas
When extending into new strategies (e.g. after-hours), verify automated stops work in that session

title: Do not skip this step with your trading

Archive winning setups in Playbook form; build your strategy from what works for you personally
Trying different setups during early development is a required step before specialization
You cannot know your strengths until you have tried and measured multiple different approaches

Once you deviate from plan emotionally, every subsequent step is also emotional - slippery slope
Trust your system's back-tested logic; temporary adverse moves after adjustments are expected

title: Don't Chase
principles: Never enter a momentum stock 3-4 days into a move without a defined stop that justifies the risk/reward
Chasing erases all prior discipline gains; one chasing loss requires 5+ good trades to recover
FOMO drives most chasing decisions; fight it with a written game plan and defined entry prices
Professionals in momentum trades have pre-defined exits and get out when momentum stops; retail chases too late
Find the breakout entry (day 0 or 1), not the follow-through (day 3-4+)

principles: When you place a bid at the mid, your own order artificially inflates the displayed mid - ignore the new mid
A 1-2 lot on the bid/ask is almost always a retail trader; large equal-sized lots on both sides = market maker
Use market maker's mid (before your own order changes it) as the true fair value for fills
Chasing artificially inflated mids can result in paying way above fair value; be patient at initial price

principles: Options volatility spike causes P&L to show worse than model predicts; this is temporary, not final

Volatility compression after a sell-off bounce restores P&L rapidly; patience during spikes is essential
Swing in outcome from panicking vs holding can be $6,000+ per trade

title: Don't Push Your Luck
principles: Never re-enter a strategy trade outside the defined trigger conditions just because it worked last time
Boredom is not a valid reason to trade; re-entering after winning causes irrational exuberance losses
A consistent strategy requires following it exactly as back-tested; improvisation destroys expectancy
Plan your trade and trade your plan; if fundamental market conditions haven't changed, trust the system

title: Don't Reinvent the Wheel
principles: When a strategy has execution problems, tweak the structure rather than abandoning the strategy
Options flexibility means most execution problems can be solved with a structural adjustment
Broken wing butterfly can solve delta-chasing issues in standard M3/iron condor setups
Solve problems within your proven strategy framework before seeking an entirely new approach

title: Don't Trade Before 10AM
principles: Options prices are artificially elevated at market open due to panic buying/selling; wait 30-60 minutes
Even if market doesn't reverse, waiting 30 minutes still yields better option prices due to volatility normalization
Exceptions: closing a winning position at abnormally good prices; margin/execution errors
Most profitable opening panic situations resolve; don't react to the very first move

title: Don't Trade Like the Three Stooges
principles: Limit simultaneous options positions to 5 or fewer so all can be managed properly in a flash crash
With 8+ positions, you cannot adjust them all during fast markets; untreated positions suffer
In calm markets position count doesn't matter; in crashes you cannot predict the timing, so stay under limit
Back-testing is meaningless if you cannot actually execute the adjustments in real market conditions

title: Don't Trap Yourself into Trading Failure
principles: Have 1-2 years of living expenses funded separately before trading full-time; do not dip into trading capital
Paper trade for at least 1-2 months before going live; live trade small until consistently profitable
Fastest path to profitability in market-neutral options: 6 months; realistic: 1-2 years
Desperately gambling a large position to recover capital is the final stage of the failure trap
Find your bread-and-butter trade first; only after months of comfort should you scale capital

title: Do Retail Traders Have a Chance?
principles: Retail traders can be consistently profitable but must trade setups that are not time-sensitive or HFT-competed
Swing trading and longer timeframes are more viable for retail than micro-scalping
Focus 90% of time on proven edge setups; 10% on finding new edge
Improvements in retail platforms (backtesting, scanning) reduce the prop advantage gap over time

title: Do THIS after a gut-wrenching trading loss
principles: Create an anti-playbook trade after bad losses: document exactly what you did wrong and commit not to repeat
Use emotional frustration after a loss as fuel for constructive analysis, not self-destruction
Anti-playbook analysis internalizes what NOT to do more effectively than reading rules
Specificity about the mistake is essential: vague frustration is wasted; precise identification creates improvement

title: Do This Before Every Covered Call Trade
principles: Only sell covered calls on stocks you are fundamentally bullish on long-term; stock decline dwarfs any premium
Sell call strike where you'd be happy selling shares at that price if called away; don't cap upside too aggressively
Never sell a covered call below your original cost basis; that trade can never recover full cost
If premium at cost-basis strike is tiny (<$36), simply wait for stock to bounce before selling next call
Consider embedded capital gains tax consequences before picking a strike that could force a taxable sale

Read what didn't happen (failed moves) rather than just reacting to what did happen

A losing trade, even if won, rarely becomes a great trade - best case is slightly positive

Risk management: know total premium at risk; have a partner watch the book when managing many positions

title: Elite Prop Trader's High Odds Breakout Technique (Step-by-Step Instructions)

setups.name: Day 3 breakout over day 2 inside accumulation day high
setups.preconditions: Strong catalyst day 1 (partnership, funding, restructuring, earnings) with big % move; stock closes strong; day 2 is an inside/low-volume consolidation day (accumulation); meaningful float short interest or tiny float; day 3 breaks above day 2 high within first 30 minutes
setups.entry_trigger: Buy the break of day 2 high; stop either few cents below the 5-minute breakout bar or low of day
setups.invalidation: Price fails to break day 2 high on open; stop hit at low of day
setups.targets: Scale 1/3 or 1/4 into momentum; trail on 2-min 9 EMA for continuation; final exit on first 5-min close below 9 EMA; always hold 10-20% as a swing piece
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Directly applicable to crypto: crypto tokens with catalyst (partnership, treasury strategy, funding) often form 2-3 day breakout patterns; use VWAP + 9 EMA trail on 2-min/5-min charts; high short interest tokens produce the best squeezes on day 3
quotes: when it works, it really works
one entry, one stop, and you leave the position alone and let it work
the day three breakout over the accumulation day high

principles: Day 2 inside/low-volume consolidation is key - it traps chasers, gives shorts confidence, and lets smart money accumulate
Simple entry + clear stop = avoids death by a thousand cuts for newer traders
Check higher time frame resistance (weekly chart) before the trade - be aware even if stock can blow through it
Volume confirmation on the breakout (top 2-3 volume bars) is the most important check for continuation
Common traits: all broke consolidation day high within 30 mins; all had strong day 1 catalyst; all had float/short interest dynamics

title: Elite Trading Requires Setting Time To Have Fun
principles: Elite trading performance requires scheduling time for fun and recovery outside of trading hours
Higher energy, focus, and open-mindedness outside market hours translates directly into better real-time decisions
Set trading goals that connect to meaningful life improvements - this is the most effective motivational exercise
Shared experiences outside of trading build stronger team bonds which improve collaborative trading
Comprehensive well-being (health, relationships, pursuits) reduces the negative impact of losing trades on performance

title: Entering a Bearish Butterfly Late in the Trading Cycle
principles: Bearish butterfly premise: markets always retrace after any rally; have maximum capital in the trade when retracement probability is highest (after a large rally)
If capital is freed late, enter the full triple-butterfly position as a fresh start at current prices rather than skipping the month
Fresh-start entry after a large rally = cheaper cost basis + higher probability of retracement than entering 8 weeks earlier
Understand the premise of every strategy; trade the premise, not the rules blindly
As the market rallies, you get closer to the inevitable retracement - that is the best time to enter the bearish butterfly

title: Essential Trade Strategies for the Week Top Stock Ideas & Execution

setups.name: Backside short on extended small cap (multi-day VWAP failure)
setups.preconditions: Small cap ran 100%+ on news; next day shows engulfing failure off the open; pre-market high rejection confirmed; sustained volume on the failure; SSR may offer a brief pop
setups.entry_trigger: Short on pop toward 2-day VWAP that fails to reclaim; or short vs. day high after failed follow-through push; hold as swing short vs. day high
setups.invalidation: Price reclaims and holds above 2-day VWAP / above the day's high
setups.targets: Trim at -30% of move; target return to near original catalyst price
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Directly applicable to crypto pump-and-dumps; use 2-day VWAP as resistance for swing shorts; SSR equivalent is just aggressive buyers on crypto - fade the secondary pop
quotes: as long as those reclaims and pops fail to hold I'm going to be looking to get short versus the day's high
wait for the turn and for a defined level to be able to risk against with confidence

setups.name: Relative strength sector long swing (breakout from consolidation)
setups.preconditions: Strong sector (e.g. biotech) making relative highs vs. market; near 52-week high breakout area; previous resistance becomes support; market stabilizing above key support level
setups.entry_trigger: Wait for market to hold key support zone then look for individual sector leaders breaking out of multi-week base with volume
setups.invalidation: Market breaks below rising 50-day or key support zone
setups.targets: Swing trade; exit on further extension or sector breakdown
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Crypto sector rotation (AI, DeFi, L2) works the same way; find the strongest coin in the strongest sector breaking out when BTC stabilizes
quotes: once I have confirmation I'll really shift my focus to include some directional long swings

principles: Cycle awareness: day-one gapers closing green signals hot small-cap environment; when vwap reclaims fail, cycle is shifting
Market internals showing change of character intraday signal high-confidence directional trades
Add aggressively on confirmation of direction; do not get too early on secondary pops of beaten-down names

title: Everything You NEED to Know Before Placing a Trade
principles: Pre-trade checklist: news catalyst, RVOL (arball), VWAP position, ATR, average volume, long-term technicals, sector ETF strength, tape/confirmation, short interest, float, institutional ownership, market context, entry/stop/target, gap %, who is in control, what type of trade (scalp/swing/breakout)
You are not prepared to trade a stock if you do not know all of these data points
Different types of trades (scalp, opening drive, trade-to-hold, swing) have different variables and must be pre-identified
Time of day matters: open = opening drives/scalps; midday = swing setups/fades; close = trend continuation
Without knowing the full details of a news catalyst you cannot properly gauge magnitude, direction, or type of move

title: Every Trader Faces THIS Issue (how to overcome it)

setups.name: VWAP pullback long (institutional support + sloped VWAP)
setups.preconditions: Stock showing strength in first 30-60 minutes; high institutional ownership (70%+); VWAP is sloped upward (not flat); stock holding above +1 standard deviation VWAP band; market / sector ETF also strong
setups.entry_trigger: Enter long on pullback to VWAP; stop 1/4 standard deviation below VWAP; look for gradual accumulation (not a spike) at VWAP - shows institutional buying
setups.invalidation: Stock spends time below VWAP or volume accumulates below VWAP
setups.targets: First 20% at +1 std dev band; hold for high-of-day and beyond using 9/21 EMA on 5-min as trail
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: VWAP pullback longs work well in crypto during trending sessions; use funding rate to confirm institutional bias; sloped VWAP on 5-min with higher lows is the key pattern
quotes: I want to see a slope of vwap that means there's a lot of volume being done above vwap
on this day on the seventh JPM never closed below the 21 EMA on the five minute

principles: Three-strike rule for over-trading: give yourself 3 attempts on a trade idea; after 3 failures on the same ticker, stop trading it for the day
Recognize emotional states that lead to over-trading (revenge trading, boredom, previous missed trade) and divert energy to research or breaks
Structure experimentation: know in advance what type of trade you are making that day; do not drift into random setups
Send daily reviews to peers for accountability even on demo/small accounts
Take only 20% off at momentum spikes when in a trade-to-hold - not half the position; give yourself a near-free trade

title: Every Trader Needs to Know This

setups.name: Intraday mean reversion short (blowoff top)
setups.preconditions: Stock/ETF makes out-of-character multi-ATR move to upside in pre-market or first 30 min; blowoff volume candle at high; price fails to follow through on multiple attempts; sellers hold VWAP after the initial spike
setups.entry_trigger: Short on break of consolidation / low of day after price has remained weak (failed to reclaim VWAP) for 45+ minutes; stop above VWAP or above intraday high
setups.invalidation: Price reclaims VWAP and makes a higher high with volume
setups.targets: Continuation to the downside; trail using VWAP as resistance; cover into new lows
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Classic crypto blowoff top pattern; pre-market multi-ATR spike followed by failure to hold VWAP is a high-probability short; works on Hyperliquid perps with confirmed tape weakness
quotes: we need price to confirm weakness and we need a change of character
failure to follow through... sellers remained present and finally we took out the low of day

setups.name: VWAP surf long (trending stock)
setups.preconditions: Stock in play with strong catalyst; breaks pre-market resistance; pulls back to VWAP; confirms higher low; holds VWAP and surfs above it with higher lows/highs
setups.entry_trigger: Enter on pullback to VWAP after confirming higher low; stop below VWAP; add on each new VWAP surf (stock not extended far above)
setups.invalidation: First close below VWAP on meaningful volume
setups.targets: Trim on significant extension above VWAP; add on every VWAP surf; hold swing piece overnight
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: VWAP surfing is highly effective in trending crypto sessions; use as the primary entry filter for momentum longs on Hyperliquid
quotes: every time price extended significantly from VWAP is where I began trimming
every time we pulled into VWAP and surfed above it and maintained a higher low, that's where I would look to add

setups.name: Consolidation breakout long (base near rising MAs)
setups.preconditions: Leading stock in leading sector; pulling back to 5/10-day SMA after a breakout; volume contracting during consolidation; clear resistance level identifiable across multiple timeframes
setups.entry_trigger: Price breaks above consolidation resistance on expanding volume; confirm on 1-min and 5-min; stop below VWAP near breakout level
setups.invalidation: Price retests breakout level and falls back below it with volume; price breaks below VWAP after the breakout
setups.targets: Hold as long as stock surfaces above VWAP and makes higher lows; sell on VWAP break
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Base-and-break patterns near rising EMAs work in crypto; ensure stock is in hottest sector theme; confirm volume expansion on break for highest-confidence entries
quotes: when volume dies down so dramatically near an all-important inflection point the outcome will be immense
not once tested VWOP close to the breakout level - that's what you want to see

principles: Price action is king over lagging indicators; indicators are useful when they align with price action to produce explosive moves
Shifting momentum signals: break of support, consecutive lower highs, severe capitulatory move, trend line break
Use multiple time frames: establish setup on daily/weekly, execute on 1-min/5-min

title: Evolution of Traders
principles: Most traders go through multiple failed strategies (newsletters, value investing, high-gamma options) before finding their niche
Psychological comfort with a strategy is the prerequisite for consistent profitability
The trial-and-error period typically takes 3-5 years; persistence through failures is essential
You will not be successful with any trading style unless you are psychologically comfortable with the risks involved
Find the trading style that matches your psychological makeup - risk tolerance is personal and cannot be forced

title: Example of Trading Edge
principles: Options credit spreads can be used to add edge to a simple 5-day high/low breakout system: they cap the upside but significantly reduce drawdowns and add theta decay income
A strategy with smaller but more consistent returns (blue equity curve) beats one with higher peak returns but massive drawdowns (orange curve) because traders actually follow through long-term
When back-testing directional systems, overlay options structures to transform erratic equity curves into smoother ones
Finding edge means finding something that works across many parameter combinations, not just one specific optimized set
Return on max drawdown is a better metric than absolute return for evaluating tradability of a strategy

title: Exit strategies for your trading to lock in more profits (be definitive!)

setups.name: Big dog (wedge/consolidation) breakout trade
setups.preconditions: Stock in play with RVOL > 2; holding above VWAP; tight consolidation (wedge or ascending triangle) forming; volume contracts during consolidation; elevated short float
setups.entry_trigger: Break above the consolidation on elevated volume; tape accelerates with large green prints; stop just below the consolidation low or VWAP
setups.invalidation: Price breaks back below VWAP or below the consolidation on volume; series of lower highs develops
setups.targets: Scale on momentum; use blow-off top signals (volume spike + wick candle + EMA break) as reason to exit; hold 10-20% for the bigger move
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Big dog breakouts work on all 24/7 markets; use 9 EMA on 1-min/5-min for trailing; crypto versions often on higher RVOL so adjust consolidation time requirement
quotes: the more time it spends in that consolidation the more significant the breakout can be
you saw what you needed to see when we lifted up there and we failed, that's a huge opportunity

principles: Define exit criteria before entering the trade - a series of lower highs, blow-off top, 5-min close below 9 EMA, or ATR target
Exit reasons should be a culmination of 2-3 factors, not just one; but pre-define the combination before the trade
Remember what type of trade you are making: trade-to-hold vs scalp require completely different exit frameworks
Be definitive about exit plans; indecision at exits is the primary cause of leaving money on the table in winning trades
Upgrade a B trade to A+ trade based on tape reading in real-time; that conviction should keep you in longer

title: Expanding Volatility

setups.name: ETF trend trade during high volatility regime
setups.preconditions: VXX breaks out of a consolidation range to the upside, signaling expanding volatility; market moves in 2-point+ increments; move to SPY/ETF trading away from individual names
setups.entry_trigger: On gap down: buy the bounce after initial flush; when bounce exhausts, wait for break of morning low then short toward pre-established intraday support; next day, look for higher low to confirm trend change
setups.invalidation: Price holds above morning high on long side; price holds above breakdown level on short side
setups.targets: Use day 1 intraday levels as day 2 targets; break of morning low targets next major support; bounce targets morning high
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Directly applicable: when crypto volatility expands (VIX analog = DVOL or funding rate spikes), shift to BTC/ETH index-equivalent; use intraday support/resistance from prior day as targets for follow-through
quotes: when volatility starts to expand we want to move to trading the market via ETFs
use levels that were established intraday, using those for day one and using those levels as targets for day two

principles: Monitor VXX/volatility ETF for regime shift signals; when it breaks out, change trading mode to ETF-focused
During high volatility, prioritize liquidity (ETFs) over individual names to better control risk
Day 1 intraday levels become day 2 targets - carry structural levels forward when in volatile trending regime

principles: Spin-off ratio and tax treatment (taxable vs. tax-free) are key facts to know before trading spin-off situations

Total combined value of parent + spun entity should approximate pre-spin value

title: Fading A Stock Up Following Earnings

setups.name: Earnings gap-up fade (disappointing beat into resistance)
setups.preconditions: Stock gaps up 5%+ on earnings; beat was modest (slight EPS beat, small guidance raise); stock is gapping into major multi-year resistance zone; low short float (no squeeze risk)
setups.entry_trigger: Offer stock in pre-market at resistance zone; re-enter short on intraday retracement to resistance (wait for seller confirmation at resistance level); stop above pre-market high + buffer
setups.invalidation: Stock holds above resistance after initial fade; breaks out to new highs
setups.targets: Morning low; then next major support level (4-5 points lower); partial cover at morning low, hold remainder as swing
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Applicable to crypto: when a token gaps up on modest news into major resistance, look for the fade; check token-equivalent of float (circulating supply vs locked); use pre-market high as stop
quotes: if a stock is gapping up a lot on something like that I'm skeptical
the first move going to be down... then i can step back and use intraday tape reading skills to find spots to re-enter

principles: Check long-term chart for resistance before fading an earnings gap-up; best risk-reward when gapping directly into multi-year supply zone
Verify short float is low before fading a gap - high short float = squeeze risk ruins the fade
Written game plan with specific entry/re-entry/stop/target before market open is essential for earnings fades
First move down = confirmation; retracement to resistance = re-entry; take partial profits at morning low, hold rest as swing

title: Fail, win and then fail some more to become a winning trader
principles: Exposure to diverse setups + experimentation is required before you can identify which setups match your strengths
The process is: exposure -> experiment -> fail -> win -> fail -> record -> build playbook
Do not copy setups; expose yourself to them and then determine which fit your personality and talent set
Eliminate setups that consistently lose for you through the recording and review process
Archive winning trades and note failing trades; build your playbook from accumulated evidence

title: Fear may be saving this trader
principles: Fear of sizing up may be protective if you have not yet measured and documented edge for a specific strategy
Only size up after a significant live track record (at least 10 sessions of consistent profitability) on the specific strategy
Measure edge by tracking trades in a performance tool (TraderView); the equity curve must be strong before requesting more capital/risk
Scale up 20% at a time (not all at once); systematic and gradual sizing increases prevent catastrophic drawdowns
Earning the right to size up = demonstrating consistent measured edge, not just feeling confident

title: February 1st Morning Meeting

setups.name: Second-day earnings continuation play
setups.preconditions: Stock gapped on earnings; consolidated in pre-market; next morning is gapping above prior after-hours high consolidation; sector is strong
setups.entry_trigger: Hold above the prior consolidation zone (23.10) by 10:30-11am; enter long on confirmation
setups.invalidation: Fails to hold above prior consolidation zone by mid-morning
setups.targets: High of prior trading session / all-time highs
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Post-earnings continuation is common in crypto too; look for tokens holding above initial catalyst level on day 2 with continued volume
quotes: this is a very nice technical setup and one that shows that after the initial move people are still interested in getting in there

setups.name: Drug/FDA announcement range play
setups.preconditions: Biotech stock with FDA news; pre-market volume 100k-500k; price establishing a range in pre-market; mini-downtrend forming from pre-market high
setups.entry_trigger: Long if mini-downtrend breaks to upside (above 66.50); short if price breaks below 65.80 consolidation
setups.invalidation: Price does not move outside established pre-market range by 10:30
setups.targets: Long: pre-market high; Short: 64 gap fill
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Analogous to crypto token with protocol upgrade news; pre-market equivalent is pre-open futures session; same framework of range extremes applies
quotes: I just need to follow the price action this mini downtrend that's developed in the pre-market

principles: Market context first: establish the SPY's key levels before trading individual names
Volume in pre-market matters: thick pre-market volume gives confidence in the setup; thin volume requires caution
On earnings plays, the prior day's consolidation level is the key level to watch the next morning

title: Feeling when it's different (reading the tape)

setups.name: Round-number break fade (tape-reading level break)
setups.preconditions: Low-float stock holding a key psychological level (e.g. $3.00); multiple failed attempts to lift off lows; buyers not able to accelerate price off support (slow tape, price lifts slowly then fails at same level repeatedly)
setups.entry_trigger: Short when the stock fails to lift above prior pop highs (e.g. $3.15-3.16) on a retest - the speed of the lift changes (slower, less urgent) compared to prior lifts; stop above $3.10 or prior pop high
setups.invalidation: Price accelerates above prior resistance ($3.15-3.16) with volume and size
setups.targets: Cover half at VWAP; move stop to break even; wait for break of $3.00 key level for second leg; cover remainder on momentum flush
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Tape reading of round-number support breaks applies directly to crypto; watch order book for large bids disappearing vs. being taken; speed and urgency of bounces off support is the key signal
quotes: that's the feeling I'm trying to describe - when it feels different
you can try it three or four times - you just have to be right once
the game is not to be perfect - it's to be right with size when it works

principles: Reading the tape is about identifying when the current behavior is DIFFERENT from the established pattern
Speed and urgency of price moves off support/resistance tells you whether buyers/sellers are committed
Distinguish whether a bid was TAKEN or just pulled - completely different implications for direction
Try the setup multiple times with small size and tight stops; only need to be right once for a good day
Pattern of behavior (how quickly it lifts, does it spray aggressively or slow-roll) builds the context for recognizing 'different'

title: Financing an Options Purchase
principles: Never think of selling short options as 'financing' a long option - you are taking on a dangerous obligation
Naked short options can wipe out months of premium income in a single gap event (e.g. flash crash)
Always ensure your number of short options does not exceed your number of long options (spread structures only)
Cash flow from short options is NOT the same as reduced risk - the obligation on the short remains
The safe structure: long option + matching short option = defined risk; never more short than long

title: Find great levels in the S&P500

setups.name: Custom volume profile level trade (high-volume / low-volume nodes)
setups.preconditions: Create a custom-period volume profile covering the current structure (e.g. from last significant gap or breakout); identify high-volume nodes (HVN) and low-volume nodes (LVN)
setups.entry_trigger: When price reaches a LVN (low volume notch), look for rejection and fade; when price approaches HVN from below, look for support; when price breaks out of LVN, expect extended continuation to next HVN
setups.invalidation: Price blasts through LVN on high volume without hesitation
setups.targets: Rotate from one extreme of the volume distribution to the other; intermediate HVN/LVN levels as partials
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Volume profile is one of the most powerful tools for crypto (Hyperliquid supports it); custom-period VP from recent structure gives the clearest tradeable levels; POC and LVN breaks are high-probability setups
quotes: areas of high volume and areas of low volume are the key levels to find
custom period composite volume profiles to find very tradable levels

principles: Custom-period volume profiles (fitted to the current market structure, not arbitrary daily/weekly resets) give the most meaningful levels
High-volume nodes = strong support/resistance; low-volume nodes = price moves quickly through (thin air)
Visually find LVNs by darkening the histogram until gaps appear - those gaps are tradeable levels

title: Finding a long term bottom in Twitter

setups.name: Long-term base retest long (beaten-down large cap)
setups.preconditions: Well-known stock beaten down 50-60% from highs; multiple tests of same support level ($14 in TWTR); negative news being bought at support; institutional/value buyers visible; fundamentals support floor (cash + revenue run rate)
setups.entry_trigger: On negative catalyst (earnings miss, downgrade) that takes price to established support: buy the hold of prior lows; risk 1-2 dollars below the support zone
setups.invalidation: Price breaks and closes significantly below established support floor
setups.targets: 50% of the total down move as primary target; speculative names can double; use earnings reports as checkpoints
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Applicable to beaten-down crypto blue chips (BTC, ETH, major L1s) at key multi-month support: look for negative news being bought at support as confirmation; risk 1-2% below support zone
quotes: at 14 you got a couple of dollars of downside... and $7 of upside
negative news being bought at support is something to take note of

principles: When a well-known stock is beaten 40-60%, it attracts a different type of buyer (value/institutional); watch for this regime change
Each earnings reaction at the same support level either strengthens or weakens the base - news being bought = strengthening base
Prior lows from crash events (e.g. Aug 2015 flash crash) become long-term targets on the recovery
50% recovery of the down move is the baseline target; doubles happen in more speculative names

title: Finding Edge in VXX

setups.name: VXX fade after ATR extension above linear regression
setups.preconditions: VXX (or UVXY / volatility product) rallies 1.5+ ATRs above 30-bar linear regression or exponential moving average; momentum or linear regression on a 2-4 bar trigger begins to roll over
setups.entry_trigger: Short when price has pulled 1.5 ATR above LR and the 2-4 bar momentum trigger rolls down; stop above recent high; manage to lower LR band or prior support
setups.invalidation: Price continues to expand above 2 ATR above LR without rolling
setups.targets: Return to LR mean; then lower band
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Applicable to DVOL (crypto volatility) or any perpetually-decaying volatility product; crypto volatility products have negative drift similar to VXX; fade rallies in DVOL using same ATR-extension methodology
quotes: when you find something that works... you don't have to be very specific about how you implement it
1 and a half atrs above linear regression... that's a decent fade signal in the market

principles: True edge exists when the strategy works across many parameter combinations, not just one optimized set - avoid curve-fitting
VXX has negative long-term drift; always short-biased; long signals have poor system-level edge
Systematic back-testing with genetic search across 1000+ parameter combinations reveals the common features of edge
Look for ATR extension from a slow mean (30-bar) with a fast trigger (2-4 bar) for the best fade signals

title: Finding Edge with This Volatility Filter
principles: Apply a volatility/range filter to any intraday strategy: only trade when the 50-bar range on a 30-min chart exceeds 1-2% - this removes low-volatility chop periods
VWAP strategies have edge on their own; the edge is dramatically enhanced by filtering for sufficient market movement
Small-range markets produce losing trades for momentum/VWAP strategies; filter them out to dramatically improve equity curve
When SPY is in a tight consolidation, shift to finding individual in-play names rather than trading the index
This type of volatility filter is simple to code and significantly improves any directional intraday system

title: Finding Your Edge
principles: Finding edge is only step one; you must find edge that highlights YOUR specific talent set (processing speed, analytical depth, patience, etc.)
Scalping, automated trading, low-float, earnings plays, second-day plays - elite traders master ONE niche that fits their personality
Use performance data (equity curves, win rates by setup) to identify which setups you actually have measurable edge in
The sequence: foundation -> experiment -> playbook -> niche -> scale up that niche consistently
Embrace technology: filters, scripts, automated trading add 20k+ per month to experienced traders by surfacing more opportunities in their niche

title: First comes...next comes...then comes...for the developing trader
principles: Correct sequence for developing traders: 1) Find setups worth studying and build your playbook, 2) Become consistent trading those setups, 3) THEN focus on sizing up
Skipping to large size before achieving consistency interrupts natural development and causes regression
Missing a trade is frustrating but over-sizing in lesser setups to compensate is a destructive pattern
P&L-based thinking (sizing up to chase losses) is the enemy of playbook-based thinking
Measuring progress by how well you execute your playbook (not by P&L) is the correct mindset for developing traders

title: Five Things Profitable Traders Do FULL WEBINAR
principles: Profitable traders try to grow (improve daily) not just make money; losing traders chase the P&L
Stock selection is foundational: news catalyst (unusual beat/miss), high RVOL, tight spread, moves away from price, above/below daily range - get this right before anything else
RVOL (ArBall) above 2 = in-play; the higher the better; always use as a stock selection filter
Embrace technology: filters, scripts, scanners add measurable P&L (documented 20k+ per day for elite traders)
Finding your niche: master one setup type that matches your talents; do it bigger and more often; slowly eliminate mediocre setups
Profitable traders use VWAP and RVOL as their two primary indicators
Discipline comes from trading your playbook, not from willpower alone; playbook-based decisions eliminate real-time indecision

title: Focus on sustainable trading strategies
principles: Red flags that suggest you got lucky (not edge): selling naked options, trading only weekly options (5-6 week winning streaks end in blowup), only live-traded without back-testing, traded only 6-9 months
Back-test across multiple market regimes (election years, crash years, trending years) to verify strategy survives adverse conditions
A strategy that only works in one type of market is not durable - you need multi-regime evidence
Before increasing capital level (personal or prop), verify: back-tested over 3-10 years, traded across different market types, bread-and-butter strategy is confirmed profitable
Never scale from 10k to 300k capital based on 6 months of live results - that is how accounts blow up

title: Forex Daily Review 7/23/12

quotes: in a range bound market when you're at the range high or range low you want to look for those failed breaks
the S&P already gave us some signs of that

Bullish bias at range lows requires treating supports differently than resistances
Range-bound markets reward patience and level-based entries; random reactionary entries destroy edge

title: Forex Forward: Weekly Analysis For Week 10.22.12
principles: Higher time frame analysis (weekly/4H) provides the framework for directional bias; lower time frames provide entry precision
Higher low + higher high structure = bullish; lower high = early warning of trend change but requires confirmation (close below key level)
Correlations across forex pairs (dollar frank vs. euro, pound vs. euro) confirm or deny directional bias before taking a trade
Treat supports differently in bullish structures - they are more likely to hold and offer better long entries than shorts

title: Forex/Futures Weekly: Holiday Expectations

setups.name: Max fake reversal trade at structural resistance
setups.preconditions: Price approaches a well-known resistance (prior swing high, psychological level) in a broader uptrend; price briefly trades above it but shows a bearish close (shooting star) on higher time frame (4H or 8H)
setups.entry_trigger: After bearish close above resistance, wait for next candle to open and take out the prior candle's low; enter short; stop above the wick high
setups.invalidation: Price makes a strong close above resistance with follow-through momentum

title: How Good Are YOUR Levels

setups.name: Market Profile Short from Sellers Zone with Partial at Intermediate Level
preconditions: Crude oil: market profile identifies sellers zone (value area high or prior distribution)
Hypothesis 1: price opens in or near sellers zone and auction fails to break higher
Pre-session levels mapped: sellers zone, intermediate S/R, primary support
setups.entry_trigger: Price enters sellers zone; fails to attract new buyers (low volume at the level); enter short on failure signal at sellers zone
setups.invalidation: Price breaks above sellers zone with expanding volume and holds; hypothesis invalidated
targets: Intermediate support as first partial (50% off); primary support as final target
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Apply to BTC perpetual: identify value area high from prior 24h market profile; if price opens at VAH and auction fails, short with target at point of control (POC) then value area low.
quotes: Wait for failure at the level before entry; the level tells you where, the price action tells you when

principles.text: Market profile levels are hypotheses, not predictions; you must observe price action at the level to confirm or invalidate before entering.
Partial profits at intermediate levels reduce risk and allow holding a runner to the full target.

title: How I Avoid False Breakouts My Secret Technique

setups.name: 5-Bar Breakout Confirmation Filter
preconditions: Stock at key breakout level (opening range high, daily resistance)
Identified setup as potential breakout trade
Market context supports direction (SPY aligned)
setups.entry_trigger: Observe 5 consecutive bars after the breakout attempt and classify each: aggressive (strong close in direction), passive (indecisive), indecisive (doji/narrow), lethargic (low volume reversal). Enter only if bar sequence shows buildup pressure on the wrong side first (false pressure), then 2+ aggressive bars confirming the real direction
setups.invalidation: Bars show lethargic or indecisive sequence after initial break; volume does not confirm
targets: Measured move equal to the range being broken; prior key resistance levels
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Direct analog for BTC/ETH breakouts: at key resistance, watch 5 candles after the test; aggressive close above + volume = enter; lethargic close or reversal candle = false breakout, fade it.
quotes: Pressure builds on the wrong side first, then the real move happens; the false breakout IS the setup

principles.text: Failed breakout as trade: when a breakout attempt produces lethargic bars and reverses, the failed breakout itself is a high-conviction trade in the opposite direction.
Fold/stand/add decision framework at breakout: fold if bars turn lethargic; stand if indecisive; add if aggressive bars confirm.

title: How I Buy Stocks At Huge Discounts with Options

principles.text: Deep ITM calls as stock surrogate: buy deep in-the-money calls (delta ~0.90) to control 100 shares with less capital; trigger is RSI oversold on daily chart combined with strong fundamental thesis.
Deep ITM calls have high delta and low time decay cost; they approximate stock ownership at a fraction of the capital outlay.

title: How I Make Money Trading Even When Im Wrong

principles.text: OTM put credit spread on SPX: sell OTM put, buy further OTM put; profit as long as index stays above short put strike at expiration; win rate high because market must only avoid falling below strike, not rally.
Credit spreads define risk and allow you to be wrong on direction (within bounds) and still profit from time decay.

title: How To Avoid A Runaway Freight Train

setups.name: Runaway Open - Wait for Retracement to Top Resistance Before Entry
preconditions: Stock with pre-defined S/R levels from morning game plan (S1/S2/R1/R2/R3 + inflection)
Open: stock immediately blows through ALL resistance levels in first 5 minutes
No short opportunity at any individual resistance level (runaway momentum)
setups.entry_trigger: After blowing through all resistance, watch for retracement back to the TOP resistance level (R3); if price holds above R3 for 15-20 minutes and consolidates, enter long for the next leg higher. Conversely, if price consolidates BELOW R2 after blowing through it then reversing, that is the signal to go short targeting the inflection.
setups.invalidation: Long: price falls below R3 on volume. Short: price reclaims R2 with volume.
targets: Long: extension beyond R3 (measured move). Short: inflection level, then S1/S2.
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: BTC: pre-define R1/R2/R3 for session; if price blows through all three in first 30 minutes, wait for retracement to R3 and hold before adding long; do not short into momentum.
quotes: If it blows through all your resistance right on the open, do not short it; wait to see if it holds the top resistance and look for the long

principles.text: Rule: if a stock blows through all resistance levels in the first 15 minutes, do not short it; wait for the retracement and confirmation of the top level holding.
Opposite rule for downside: if price blows through all support levels immediately, do not buy; wait for retracement to bottom support and failure to confirm the short.

title: How to AVOID Getting STOPPED OUT of Great Trades

3:1 reward-to-risk on the ITM call credit spread: if market closes below the short strike (bearish thesis correct), keep entire credit; if market closes above long strike (wrong), lose fixed amount; fake-outs cannot force you out mid-trade.

title: How to avoid going on tilt while trading

principles.text: Emotions as trading signals: frustration and huffiness at an overextended stock is itself a setup signal (Bella Fade); use the emotion as a trigger to hyperfocus, not to step away.
External vs. internal frustration: frustration at market participants (external) is productive and can sharpen focus; frustration at yourself (internal) is tilt risk — redirect immediately.
Emotion-energy matching: if emotional energy is high but market opportunity is low, recognize the mismatch and reduce activity; overconfidence from a winning streak is as dangerous as despair.

Anchoring technique (Dr. Steenbarger): practice trades while in an ideal calm state; that state becomes anchored to good decisions; invoke it in real time by purposely evoking the calm state before entering.

title: How to Backtest a Trading Strategy Getting Started

principles.text: Backtest process: ask the question → design the test → analyze results → iterate; never skip steps or data-mine (build strategy first, then test on separate data).

52-week high breakout backtest result: ~50/50 win rate on breakout long; short side (fade the new high) performs better in high-beta names; neither strategy is plug-and-chug without further iteration.
Automation as complement to discretion: automate systematic entries (e.g., buy when price breaks 52-week high); use discretion for sizing and exits; hybrid approach captures both edge sources.
Data validation is critical in backtesting: always verify the data returned matches what was requested (correct date range, correct symbol) before trusting results.

setups.invalidation: Bounce closes above resistance level with volume — potential reversal, not just bounce
targets: New lows below the breakdown point
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Dead-cat bounces in crypto post-breakdown are extremely common; use 1h/4h chart; declining funding rate during bounce confirms short bias.
quotes: dead-cat bounces always look convincing until they fail at the level — that's your entry

principles.text: After any significant loss, reconstruct the trade completely: what was the actual thesis, what changed, and when did you know? The answer tells you what to fix in process.
Changing fundamentals create the best short opportunities because momentum traders who bought the story are now trapped and must sell.

title: Learn How to Use Two Effective Trading Indicators: VWAP & AVWAP

setups.name: VWAP Pullback Long (Intraday)
preconditions: Stock trending above VWAP after strong open

setups.invalidation: Price closes below VWAP on volume — institutional sellers in control
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: VWAP is calculated the same way for crypto; anchoring to daily session open gives identical pullback-to-VWAP long setups on BTC/ETH/altcoins; especially reliable during strong trend days.
quotes: VWAP is where institutions transact — a pullback to VWAP that holds tells you institutions are still buying

setups.name: Anchored VWAP Second-Day Play
preconditions: Stock had a significant catalyst (earnings, news) on day 1

Second day price trades above anchored VWAP
setups.entry_trigger: Long on second day when price pulls back to anchored VWAP from catalyst date and holds; enter on reclaim with volume
setups.invalidation: Price closes below the anchored VWAP — catalyst buyers underwater and selling
targets: 1.5× ATR extension from anchored VWAP support
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Anchor VWAP to major crypto events: token unlocks, listings, protocol launches. Second-day (or week) pullback to that anchored VWAP is a high-probability long entry.
quotes: the anchored VWAP from the catalyst date tells you the average price of everyone who bought on the news — if it holds, they're supporting it

principles.text: VWAP is not a target — it is a reference for institutional order flow; if price is above VWAP, longs are in control; below VWAP, sellers are in control.
Brian Shannon: most powerful use of AVWAP is anchoring to the most significant price event (IPO, earnings, breakout) to track the average cost basis of event-driven buyers.

title: Learning to Take a Loss

principles.text: Accepting a loss quickly at a predefined stop is a skill that must be practiced; hesitation to take losses is the root cause of account-destroying drawdowns.
Separating ego from the trade: a stopped-out trade is not a personal failure; it is the cost of doing business in a probabilistic game.

title: Learning to Take a Loss (Options)

principles.text: Options traders who cannot take a loss at the defined stop end up holding positions to expiration worthless; same principle applies to any defined-risk instrument.
The pain of taking a loss is temporary; the pain of a large loss that was avoidable through discipline is long-lasting and affects future decision-making.

title: Lessons from an Annual Trade Review

principles.text: Annual review process: categorize all trades by setup type, measure win rate and average R per setup, identify which setups to add/remove for next year.
The best traders improve through systematic review, not through trying harder; data from your own trading is the most valuable information you have.

title: Lessons from the Options Tribe Trading Contest

principles.text: Contest winners focused on high-probability setups with defined risk; contest losers swung for home runs with oversized positions — same lesson applies to any trading competition.
Drawdown protection is more important than maximizing upside in any competition or account management context; survive first, grow second.

title: Lessons on 2018 Trading Goals from the Desk

principles.text: Annual trading goals must be specific and measurable: 'improve win rate by 5%' is better than 'trade better'; attach metrics to every goal.
Daily report card: score your process execution (preparation, patience, discipline) separately from P&L; consistent process scores predict long-term P&L improvement.

title: Level 2 Strategies Every Day Trader MUST Know

1-2% from core entry for intraday scalp component

quotes: Apple would come back to the bid, get accumulated, and then push — I kept building my core until I was full size at a good average

principles.text: Level 2 reads the current supply/demand imbalance in real time; charts show the past, Level 2 shows the present — use both.

title: Level 2 Trading Secrets: How to Read the Tape Using Time & Sales

principles.text: Pre-trade checklist before reading tape: (1) check vitals — is the stock in play? (2) check chart — what are the key levels? (3) read T&S — who is in control right now?
Reading the tape is a skill that requires hundreds of hours of observation before it becomes automatic; start with one liquid stock and study it for a month.

principles.text: 4:1 reward-to-risk minimum for swing trades: if the setup doesn't offer at least 4:1, pass — the math requires it for a positive expectancy system at typical win rates.
Initiate the swing trade at the earliest confirmation point to maximize R; waiting for too much confirmation destroys the reward-to-risk ratio.

setups.name: trend_day_continuation
setups.preconditions: Confirmed breakout from multi-week/month consolidation on elevated volume (2 standard deviation volume bar). Strong macro or technical context supporting sustained trend. Lower VIX or trending environment favoring wider stops.
setups.entry_trigger: Break of consolidation range on high volume; opening drive continuation; bar trail or ATR trail establishes dynamic stop below prior bar low (long) or above prior bar high (short).
setups.invalidation: Price closes below 10-day SMA (swing trades). Price closes below prior bar low on momentum trades (bar trail exit). ATR trail breached on bar close.
setups.targets: No fixed profit target; trail via bar trail (2-min for pure momentum scalps, 5-min for opening drives, 15-min for full trend day) or ATR trail (3-period, 3x factor on 5-min chart for trend holds). Hold until trail breached.
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Directly applicable to crypto perps. Use ATR trail on 5-min or 15-min chart for BTC/ETH trend days. Bar trail on 2-min for momentum breakouts on altcoins. 10-day SMA trail for swing entries on spot/perps.
quotes: a trailing stop can provide a system that helps us hold well in trending stocks and realize significantly more profit
the type of trade that you are applying it to matters and the kind of trail that you use matters

setups.name: imbalance_scalp
setups.preconditions: Opening range breakout or momentum break with 2 standard deviation volume bar. Context of significant breakout level (e.g. SMCI backside short with opening range break).
setups.entry_trigger: Break of opening range or key intraday level on elevated volume. Enter on the break.
setups.invalidation: Prior 2-min bar low broken (for longs) or prior 2-min bar high broken (for shorts) on bar trail. Exit intrabar if pure momentum setup — do not wait for close.
setups.targets: Trail using prior 2-min bars; exit when price prints beyond prior bar high (short) or prior bar low (long). Short-duration trade.
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: 2-min bar trail works on BTC/ETH and high-volume altcoin perps during high-volume opening ranges or news-driven momentum breaks.

setups.name: liquidity_sweep
setups.preconditions: Strong in-play stock sells off quickly on the open — not a wick, but a sustained forced/sloppy sell with bars pressing lower without natural bouncing. Implies an aggressive large sell order seeking liquidity.
setups.entry_trigger: Seller lifts (visible on tape) or trendline break to the upside on the chart after the forced selldown. Enter long on the trend line break. Risk 2 cents below low of day. Two-wave target structure.
setups.invalidation: New low of day below the entry bar low. If the seller re-engages after the trend line break, exit immediately.
setups.targets: Sell half into first wave higher (momentum spike and pause). Sell second half into second wave higher (second spike and pause).
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Directly applicable to crypto perps. Forced sells from liquidations or stop-hunts below key levels create the same sloppy selloff structure. Trade the recovery once the liquidation cascade lifts. Use tape (order flow) or 30-sec chart trend line break as trigger.
quotes: the best part about this is since it's a strong stock when that order is done the stock's natural strength will take over and revert back to the upside
all we're looking for is that sloppy urgent seller to lift because once they lift our Bella fade scalp starts

setups.name: imbalance_scalp
setups.preconditions: Inplay stock establishes a trending move in one direction then consolidates into a range with at least two distinct tests of highs (or lows). Range forms near VWAP — above VWAP shorting range top, below VWAP longing range bottom. Traders on the wrong side are trapped.
setups.entry_trigger: Price attempts to break range high (or low) for second time and fails. Sellers (or buyers) respond methodically after the failed break, confirming the trapped traders thesis. Enter short (or long) on the range break in the direction of the trend, risking against the high of the failed breakout candle.
setups.invalidation: Price breaks range in the attempted direction and holds. Trapped trader thesis is wrong.
setups.targets: One measured move from the range width below the range low (for short). Shot clock: expect completion in roughly half the time it took to build the range.
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Extremely common in crypto perps: VWAP-anchored range breakout failures with trapped longs (or shorts) drive fast, clean measured moves. Use 1-min or 2-min chart. Works especially well on BTC, ETH, and high-liquidity altcoin perps.
quotes: it's actually the response to the attempt higher that gives us our scalp
our shot clock for the scalp is actually typically about half the time of that range formed

title: Zoom shows us what to do in Peloton (Trading Strategy)

setups.name: relative_strength
setups.preconditions: Two stocks in the same sector/theme (stay-at-home: ZM and PTON) trade with very similar intraday price action. Leader (ZM) begins to break down from a failed range breakout while lagger (PTON) is still pressing highs. Both are extended from multi-month uptrends. Prior day showed blow-off top behavior and first significant sell in months.
setups.entry_trigger: Leader (ZM) breaks intraday VWAP and prior support (575 level) and makes new low of day. Lagger (PTON) is still pressing highs — enter short on lagger when it fails to hold the breakout attempt (wedge failure above 131.50, wick rejection). 20-30 second window between leader breakdown and lagger following.
setups.invalidation: Lagger breaks above intraday high and holds (above 132 with follow-through volume). Leader recovers and reclaims VWAP.
setups.targets: Prior low of range (~127-128 area); measure is approximately full ATR. Cover into flush of new lows; exit when tape shows buyers at key levels. 5-minute trade expected.
setups.crypto_adaptation_notes: Directly applicable to crypto baskets. BTC leads, altcoins lag — if BTC breaks support while a correlated altcoin (ETH, SOL, etc.) is still pressing highs, fade the lagger. Also works within sector: if one L1 breaks down, fade the correlated L1 that hasn't yet responded. Use same 20-30 second window.
